apple-seed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A specialty liquid oil that can contribute a soft, mild-feeling quality in a blended bar. As a liquid oil, it does not provide the firming role of solid fats.
apple-seed-oil.workabilityNote: Check that the product is neat apple seed oil, not an extract or an infused carrier oil.
apple-seed-oil.seoSummary: a liquid specialty oil for blended bars

apricot-kernel-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid oil that can add a mild, smooth feel to a blended cold-process bar. It is not a hard-oil or big-bubble substitute on its own.
apricot-kernel-oil.workabilityNote: It blends like other liquid oils; confirm the product is apricot kernel oil before recalculating a substitution.
apricot-kernel-oil.seoSummary: a soft liquid oil for mild-feeling blends

argan-oil.coldProcessEffect: A liquid specialty oil suited to a supporting role in a blend; it contributes softness rather than the firmness or large bubbles associated with some solid fats.
argan-oil.workabilityNote: Match the supplier's exact argan oil and keep its own SAP reference when changing an existing recipe.
argan-oil.seoSummary: a specialty liquid oil for blended soap

avocado-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid oil used in blended bars for a mild, conditioned feel. It generally traces more slowly than hard fats and will not firm a recipe by itself.
avocado-oil.workabilityNote: A familiar blending oil; check the supplier's grade and recalculate lye whenever the oil changes.
avocado-oil.seoSummary: a soft liquid oil for mild, conditioned bars

babassu-oil.coldProcessEffect: Its lauric-rich profile can contribute firm bars and abundant bubbles, with cleansing character similar to—but not identical to—coconut oil.
babassu-oil.workabilityNote: Melt the solid oil fully and use its own SAP reference; do not substitute coconut-oil values.
babassu-oil.seoSummary: a firm, bubbly soap oil distinct from coconut

borage-oil.coldProcessEffect: A delicate, unsaturated liquid oil for specialty blends. It adds softness rather than bar structure; a formula's freshness and oxidation resistance matter.
borage-oil.workabilityNote: Buy a fresh, well-stored product, identify it precisely, and avoid relying on it as the bar's main hardening oil.
borage-oil.seoSummary: a delicate liquid oil best suited to specialty blends

canola-oil-high-oleic.coldProcessEffect: This high-oleic liquid oil can support a mild-feeling, slower-moving batter. Like other liquid oils, it contributes less firmness than solid fats.
canola-oil-high-oleic.workabilityNote: Verify the high-oleic grade; ordinary and high-oleic canola have different fatty-acid profiles.
canola-oil-high-oleic.seoSummary: a high-oleic liquid oil for mild soap blends

carrot-seed-oil-cold-pressed.coldProcessEffect: A specialty seed oil that behaves as a liquid blend ingredient; do not assume it will add a lasting carrot color or scent to finished soap.
carrot-seed-oil-cold-pressed.workabilityNote: Check the label carefully: this entry is cold-pressed fatty seed oil, not carrot-seed essential oil or an infusion.
carrot-seed-oil-cold-pressed.seoSummary: a specialty seed oil, not carrot essential oil

castor-oil.coldProcessEffect: Castor oil can support a stable, creamy lather in a balanced recipe. Its thick, sticky batter can become difficult to pour when castor dominates the oil blend.
castor-oil.workabilityNote: Measure carefully: castor oil is unusually viscous. A single-oil castor batch behaves very differently from a normal blend.
castor-oil.seoSummary: a thick oil used to support creamy, stable lather

cocoa-butter.coldProcessEffect: This room-temperature solid butter can add firmness and a creamy lather to a blended bar; it does not create the fluffy bubbles of lauric-rich oils.
cocoa-butter.workabilityNote: Melt fully and combine evenly with the liquid oils before making the lye calculation.
cocoa-butter.seoSummary: a firm butter for harder bars and creamy lather

coconut-oil-76.coldProcessEffect: Coconut oil can add firmness, large fluffy bubbles, and a more cleansing feel. A formula's overall balance matters; the ingredient alone does not predict the finished bar.
coconut-oil-76.workabilityNote: Melt and mix evenly; use the 76-degree product's own SAP, not values for fractionated coconut oil.
coconut-oil-76.seoSummary: a firming oil known for large, fluffy bubbles

cupuacu-butter.coldProcessEffect: A firm plant butter that can add structure and a creamy quality to a blended cold-process bar.
cupuacu-butter.workabilityNote: Melt completely and identify the supplier's exact butter grade; cupuaçu is not interchangeable with cocoa or shea butter.
cupuacu-butter.seoSummary: a firm plant butter for structured soap blends

evening-primrose-oil.coldProcessEffect: A delicate liquid seed oil suited to specialty blends. It contributes a softer feel rather than the firmness and fluffy lather of hard oils.
evening-primrose-oil.workabilityNote: Check freshness and storage history, and verify the exact supplier specification before using its reference SAP.
evening-primrose-oil.seoSummary: a delicate liquid seed oil for specialty blends

fractionated-coconut-oil.coldProcessEffect: This liquid caprylic/capric oil does not have the same lauric-rich profile as regular coconut oil, so it will not reproduce the same lather and cleansing role.
fractionated-coconut-oil.workabilityNote: Confirm the product is caprylic/capric triglycerides. Never swap in 76-degree coconut oil's SAP value.
fractionated-coconut-oil.seoSummary: a specialty liquid oil unlike solid coconut oil

grapeseed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A light, unsaturated liquid oil that can make a bar softer. Its high-linoleic profile makes freshness and oxidation considerations important in a formula.
grapeseed-oil.workabilityNote: Use a fresh, properly stored product and keep the exact grade in mind when reformulating.
grapeseed-oil.seoSummary: a light liquid oil whose freshness matters in soap

hemp-seed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft, unsaturated liquid oil for blended recipes; it contributes less firmness than room-temperature solid fats.
hemp-seed-oil.workabilityNote: Protect this delicate oil from heat, light, and air, and distinguish plain seed oil from blended hemp products.
hemp-seed-oil.seoSummary: a delicate liquid seed oil for blended bars

jojoba-oil-golden.coldProcessEffect: Jojoba is a liquid wax ester, not a typical triglyceride oil. Its unusual composition means it does not behave like common soapmaking oils.
jojoba-oil-golden.workabilityNote: Use only a jojoba-specific SAP reference and test cautiously; its very low saponification value and unusual behavior make substitutions tricky.
jojoba-oil-golden.seoSummary: a liquid wax ester with unusual soapmaking behavior

kokum-butter.coldProcessEffect: A very firm plant butter that can contribute structure and a harder feel to a blended bar.
kokum-butter.workabilityNote: Break up and melt fully before blending; confirm the exact butter because its reference SAP differs from other butters.
kokum-butter.seoSummary: a very firm butter for structured soap bars

kukui-nut-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid nut oil for blended recipes. It contributes less bar firmness than solid fats, so the full formula determines hardness and cure behavior.
kukui-nut-oil.workabilityNote: Check that the oil is fresh and confirm its botanical/product identity in the supplier specification.
kukui-nut-oil.seoSummary: a soft liquid nut oil for blended soap

mango-butter.coldProcessEffect: A room-temperature solid butter that can increase firmness and contribute a creamy lather in a balanced blend.
mango-butter.workabilityNote: Melt completely and weigh accurately; mango butter's SAP is not the same as shea or cocoa butter.
mango-butter.seoSummary: a firming butter with a creamy lather profile

marula-oil.coldProcessEffect: A liquid specialty oil for balanced blends. Its liquid-oil character adds softness rather than the firmness or large bubbles supplied by hard fats.
marula-oil.workabilityNote: Match the supplier's exact marula oil and recalculate lye if replacing another ingredient.
marula-oil.seoSummary: a specialty liquid oil for balanced blends

moringa-seed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A high-oleic liquid oil that can suit a mild-feeling blend. It remains a soft oil, so the complete formula provides the bar's structure.
moringa-seed-oil.workabilityNote: Choose the pressed seed oil, not a botanical extract, and verify the product's stated grade.
moringa-seed-oil.seoSummary: a high-oleic liquid seed oil for soap blends

murumuru-butter.coldProcessEffect: A hard, lauric-rich butter that can contribute a firm bar and abundant lather. Its SAP is notably different from many common butters.
murumuru-butter.workabilityNote: Melt thoroughly and recheck the exact supplier SAP; do not substitute a generic butter value.
murumuru-butter.seoSummary: a hard, high-SAP butter for bubbly soap

neem-oil.coldProcessEffect: A liquid specialty oil with a strong, distinctive odor that may remain noticeable in finished soap. It contributes softness, not bar structure.
neem-oil.workabilityNote: Plan for its strong natural scent and verify that the product is neem seed oil rather than an extract or blend.
neem-oil.seoSummary: a strongly scented liquid specialty oil

oat-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid oil that can add a mild-feeling quality to a blend; it does not provide the firming effect of solid fats.
oat-oil.workabilityNote: This entry is oat-derived oil, not colloidal oatmeal, oat extract, or oat protein; confirm the supplier's exact product.
oat-oil.seoSummary: a soft oat-derived oil, not colloidal oatmeal

olive-oil.coldProcessEffect: Olive oil contributes a mild-feeling bar and a small, dense lather. A high-olive recipe can trace slowly and may need extra time to harden and cure.
olive-oil.workabilityNote: A familiar liquid oil, but patience may be needed before unmolding and during the cure of olive-heavy recipes.
olive-oil.seoSummary: a mild-feeling oil that can make slow-tracing soap

olive-oil-pomace.coldProcessEffect: Pomace olive oil contributes a mild-feeling bar with dense lather, much like other olive-oil soaps. It can behave differently from other grades during mixing.
olive-oil-pomace.workabilityNote: Identify the pomace grade and follow a recipe designed for it; do not assume every olive oil has identical handling or SAP.
olive-oil-pomace.seoSummary: an olive-oil grade for mild, dense-lather soap

palm-kernel-flakes-hydrogenated.coldProcessEffect: These hard flakes can add firmness and large bubbles, like other lauric-rich fats. They are a distinct grade and do not share every palm-oil property.
palm-kernel-flakes-hydrogenated.workabilityNote: Melt fully and confirm hydrogenation and product identity; regular palm kernel oil and palm fruit oil are different ingredients.
palm-kernel-flakes-hydrogenated.seoSummary: hard palm-kernel flakes for bubbly soap

palm-kernel-oil.coldProcessEffect: Palm kernel oil can contribute firmness, large bubbles, and a more cleansing feel because of its lauric-rich profile.
palm-kernel-oil.workabilityNote: Melt and stir thoroughly; distinguish kernel oil from palm fruit oil and hydrogenated palm-kernel flakes.
palm-kernel-oil.seoSummary: a lauric-rich oil for firm, bubbly soap

palm-oil.coldProcessEffect: Palm fruit oil can add firmness and a stable, creamy lather to a blended bar. It is different from palm kernel oil, which has a more bubbly profile.
palm-oil.workabilityNote: If the container separates, mix it evenly before weighing; verify that the product is palm fruit oil.
palm-oil.seoSummary: a firming oil with stable, creamy lather

plum-kernel-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid specialty oil that can add a silky quality to a blended bar; it does not replace the hardening role of solid fats.
plum-kernel-oil.workabilityNote: Check that the seller means plum kernel oil, not an extract, and use the specific supplier's SAP information.
plum-kernel-oil.seoSummary: a soft specialty oil for silky soap blends

raspberry-seed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A delicate, unsaturated liquid oil for specialty blends. It contributes softness, while freshness and oxidation resistance should be considered.
raspberry-seed-oil.workabilityNote: Use a fresh, well-stored product and confirm the seed oil rather than a fruit extract or scented oil.
raspberry-seed-oil.seoSummary: a delicate liquid seed oil for specialty soap

rice-bran-oil.coldProcessEffect: A versatile liquid oil used in blended cold-process recipes for a mild, conditioned feel. It does not add the same firmness as palm or cocoa butter.
rice-bran-oil.workabilityNote: A useful blending oil; this reference applies to refined rice bran oil, so check the supplier's grade.
rice-bran-oil.seoSummary: a versatile liquid oil for mild soap blends

rosehip-seed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A delicate liquid seed oil best used as a specialty blend ingredient. It adds softness rather than a firm bar structure.
rosehip-seed-oil.workabilityNote: Buy fresh, store carefully, and confirm that the product is pressed seed oil rather than an infused preparation.
rosehip-seed-oil.seoSummary: a delicate specialty oil for blended soap

safflower-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid oil; high-oleic and conventional high-linoleic safflower can behave differently in soap and have different shelf-life considerations.
safflower-oil.workabilityNote: Identify whether the oil is high oleic or conventional, then match its SAP reference and freshness needs.
safflower-oil.seoSummary: a liquid oil whose safflower grade matters

shea-butter.coldProcessEffect: A solid plant butter that can add firmness and a creamy, dense lather to a blend, balancing softer liquid oils.
shea-butter.workabilityNote: Melt fully, blend evenly, and check whether the supplier's raw or refined grade matches the recipe.
shea-butter.seoSummary: a firming butter for creamy, dense lather

shea-oil-fractionated.coldProcessEffect: A liquid, processed shea ingredient that behaves differently from whole shea butter; do not expect the same solid-fat contribution to firmness.
shea-oil-fractionated.workabilityNote: Confirm the fractionation and product specification. Its SAP must not be replaced with the whole-shea-butter value.
shea-oil-fractionated.seoSummary: a liquid shea ingredient unlike whole shea butter

sunflower-oil.coldProcessEffect: A liquid oil for blended cold-process soap. High-oleic and high-linoleic sunflower types differ in fatty-acid profile, firmness, and storage considerations.
sunflower-oil.workabilityNote: Check the variety on the supplier label; identify whether it is high oleic before changing a formula.
sunflower-oil.seoSummary: a liquid soapmaking oil with grade-dependent properties

sweet-almond-oil.coldProcessEffect: A soft liquid oil that can bring a mild, smooth feel to a balanced blend. It contributes less firmness than solid fats.
sweet-almond-oil.workabilityNote: Straightforward to blend; this is sweet-almond carrier oil, not bitter almond essential oil.
sweet-almond-oil.seoSummary: a mild-feeling liquid oil for blended bars

tamanu-oil.coldProcessEffect: A liquid specialty oil with a distinct natural odor that can affect the scent of finished soap. It adds no solid-fat structure by itself.
tamanu-oil.workabilityNote: Plan for its characteristic scent and confirm that the supplier's product and SAP match this tamanu-oil entry.
tamanu-oil.seoSummary: a specialty liquid oil with a distinct natural scent

watermelon-seed-oil.coldProcessEffect: A light liquid seed oil for specialty blends. Like other soft oils, it adds little firmness on its own.
watermelon-seed-oil.workabilityNote: Confirm the product is pressed watermelon seed oil rather than a fruit extract or fragrance.
watermelon-seed-oil.seoSummary: a light liquid seed oil for soap blends

wheat-germ-oil.coldProcessEffect: A rich liquid germ oil that can contribute softness in a blend. Its tendency to oxidize makes freshness and finished-bar storage important.
wheat-germ-oil.workabilityNote: Check the harvest/product date and store it carefully; do not treat it as a hard butter or assume it lengthens shelf life.
wheat-germ-oil.seoSummary: a rich liquid oil where freshness matters
